slides.title: 14.1.1 Traversing by Distance Layers
keyPoints: Initialize all distances as unseen, set the source distance to zero, and enqueue the source.
When removing a vertex, inspect each outgoing neighbor.
For an unseen neighbor, assign the current distance plus one and enqueue it immediately.
Marking when enqueued prevents several parents from scheduling the same vertex repeatedly.
slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 14, treat 14.1.1 Traversing by Distance Layers as an algorithmic claim. Initialize all distances as unseen, set the source distance to zero, and enqueue the source. When removing a vertex, inspect each outgoing neighbor. For an unseen neighbor, assign the current distance plus one and enqueue it immediately. Marking when enqueued prevents several parents from scheduling the same vertex repeatedly. The queue contains vertices from at most two consecutive distance layers at the transition between layers. Every vertex in layer d is removed before any vertex in layer d+1 that it discovers can get ahead of it. This is why a newly discovered neighbor receives the smallest possible hop count rather than merely the first arbitrary path length. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 14, treat 14.2.1 Traversing Recursive Graph Structure as an algorithmic claim. The directed traversal uses three colors: unseen, active, and finished. On entry it marks a vertex active. An edge to another active vertex closes a path back into the current recursion chain and therefore identifies a cycle. An edge to a finished vertex does not by itself prove a cycle; two branches may legitimately converge on completed work. After every outgoing neighbor has been considered without finding a cycle, the vertex becomes finished. The outer loop starts a traversal at each still-unseen vertex so disconnected regions are not ignored. An empty graph has no directed cycle, while a self-loop reaches the current active vertex immediately. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. slides.title: Failure clinic — Visited did not mean finished
keyPoints: A directed acyclic convergence is reported as cyclic.
Inspect whether the implementation uses one boolean for both active and completed vertices.
Replace that collapsed state with the three-state model and preserve the active recursion path until outgoing work.
A BFS queue grows with many duplicate copies of the same vertex.
slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 14, treat Failure clinic — Visited did not mean finished as an algorithmic claim. A directed acyclic convergence is reported as cyclic. Inspect whether the implementation uses one boolean for both active and completed vertices. Replace that collapsed state with the three-state model and preserve the active recursion path until outgoing work is complete. A BFS queue grows with many duplicate copies of the same vertex. Check whether discovery is marked only when dequeued. Marking before enqueue prevents another predecessor from scheduling the same vertex again. This change repairs the work invariant as well as reducing redundant storage. A weighted route with fewer hops is reported as the cheapest route. The traversal can be correct for hop count while the application asked for total weight. Change the algorithm and its preconditions rather than relabeling the BFS distance as cost. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. Ask what invariant is preserved, what state changes, why termination follows, what input size controls cost, and what output or diagnostic proves the implementation matched the specification.
